data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"As n grows, the probability of reaching unanimous consensus tends to 0. The finite obstruction structures are exactly the locally stable mixed configurations: every vertex agrees with the majority of its three neighbors, equivalently each vertex has at most one neighbor of the opposite color, so the bichromatic edges form a matching and each color class induces a subgraph of minimum degree at least 2 (a 2-core). In a random 3-regular graph the typical obstructions are the 2-cores of the two initial color classes; each such 2-core is critical with expected number of vertices \u0398(n^{1/3}), so both are nonempty with high probability and consensus is blocked. Prevalence of such obstructions scales as \u0398(n^{1/3}) vertices per color class and \u0398(n^{1/3}) cross edges.","counterconditions":[{"case":"Fails if the 2-core of a Binomial(3,1/2) random induced subgraph is empty with probability bounded away from 0.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"Fails if asynchronous order can destroy a nonempty 2-core (it cannot, since each core vertex always has at least two same-color neighbors).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"Fails if the random 3-regular graph has no such 2-core whp.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The number of monochromatic edges is nondecreasing under updates (a flip increases it by 1 or 3), so the process reaches a fixed point. A fixed point is exactly a 2-core partition. The initial color class is a random induced subgraph with degree distribution Binomial(3,1/2); its 2-core is at criticality because E[D(D-1)]/E[D]=1, giving 2-core size \u0398(n^{1/3}) and nonempty whp. Any nonempty 2-core is frozen, so consensus requires at least one initial color class to have empty 2-core, which has probability o(1).","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
